In summary, our research is concerned with
the competitive adsorption of carbon dioxide (CO 2) and methane (CH 4) in clay minerals.
the competitive adsorption of CO _{2} and CH _{4} in clay rich shale formations at microscopic scale.

the competitive adsorption behavior of methane (CH(4)) and carbon dioxide (Co(2)) in montmorillonitie clay, and the effects of clay pore size and water density on adsorption capacity, isosteric adsorptin heat and selectivity are investigated using the combined molecular dynamic (MD) and grand canonical Monte Carle (GCMC) simulations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CO2/ CH4 competitive adsorption in Na montmorillonites is dominated by the adsorbability factor in dry clays, while both adsorbability and volumetric factors are involved in the wet clays, and the adsorption selectivity is enhanced with increasing pore heterogeneity caused either by the clay pore size reduction or water content increment.
the CO2/ CH4 adsorption selectivities are enhanced with increasing clay pore heterogeneity and decreasing water content in clay models, which is mainly due to the enhanced adsorbability of CO2.

the Na montorillonite clay favors CO2 over CH 4 adsorption, and the preferentially adsorbed CO 2 reduces with increasing pressure and pore size, while it increases with increasing pore heterogeneity and water density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CO2/Na+-montmorillonite clay system is a promising candidate for CO2 sequestering in shale gas reservoirs.
the clay pore size, pore heterogeneity and interlayer water content play a significant role in controlling CO2/CH _{4}  adsorption capacity, selectivity and isotherm shape.

the Na+ distribution in clay interlayer and its interaction with CO2 and substituted Al atoms play a key role in CO2/CH _{4} competitive adsorption in clay, and the water content in interlayer is a potential way to improve CS EGR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clay pore size and structure heterogeneity, which is related to water content, have important effects on the CO2/ CH4 adsorption capacity and selectivity.
the Na montorillonite clay favors preferential adsorption for CO2 over CH 4, and the selectivity of CO2 over methane increases with increasing clay pore heterogeneity and decreasing clay pore size.

the Na montomillonite clay favors preferential adsorption for CO2 over CH 4, and the selectivity of CO 2/CH 4 adsorption is mainly contributed by the adsorbility factor, which is enhanced by increasing pore heterogeneity.
